question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer implements an FCoE Unified Fabric where vPC exists between N9K-A and N9K-B. To avoid rate discards, bandwidth must be regulated to account for sent traffic that exceeds the access speed. Which set of commands completes the configuration?
context: Topology: N9K-A and N9K-B connect to SAN A / LAN / SAN B clouds via Po1, with Po10 connecting downstream via FCoE/FC/Ethernet links.
imageNote: Diagram: N9K-A and N9K-B connect to SAN A / LAN / SAN B clouds via Po1, with Po10 connecting downstream to a server via FCoE (Ethernet/FC/FCoE link types shown in legend).
options:
fcoe cost 255 on N9K-A
random-detect min 10 max 20
spanning-tree port type edge on Po10

fcoe cost 0 on N9K-A
shape min 0 gbps max 1 gbps
spanning-tree port type edge on Po1

fcoe fcf-priority 0 on N9K-A
hardware qos fc rate-shaper low
spanning-tree port type edge trunk on Po10

fcoe fcf-priority 255 on N9K-A
police 50000
spanning-tree port type edge trunk on Po1
theory: When a vPC pair of FCoE switches (N9K-A/N9K-B) uplinks FCoE traffic, the switches need to be positioned to be a preferred FCF (fcoe fcf-priority 0), rate-shape FC traffic to prevent rate discards when sent traffic momentarily exceeds the access-link speed ('hardware qos fc rate-shaper low'), and treat the downstream port channel as an edge trunk port for spanning tree so it comes up immediately without delay ('spanning-tree port type edge trunk on Po10') - combining FCF preference, hardware-based FC rate shaping, and fast STP edge behavior is what avoids the described rate discards on this unified fabric. (Cisco Nexus 9000 FCoE/vPC Configuration Guide / web research)
